newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BELLSOUTH, SAFRA SIGN UP FOR BRAZIL B BAND DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BELLSOUTH, SAFRA SIGN UP FOR BRAZIL B BAND DEAL.

text.p: A group led by BellSouth Corp and Brazilian bank Banco Safra signed up Wednesday for a multi-billion-dollar concession to provide cellular services in Sao Paulo city, one of the world's most lucrative markets.

"Sao Paulo is ahead of even Tokyo in terms of demographic density. It's as if Manhattan were multiplied several times over," said Roberto Peon, president of BellSouth Latin America after the signing ceremony in Brazil's presidential palace.

The BCP group, in which BellSouth and Safra each have a 44.5 percent stake, stunned competitors and market analysts in July when it bid 2.6 billion reais ($2.45 billion) for the 15-year B Band concession, over four times the government's asking price.
BCP officials have said Sao Paulo was worth the price given its potential for growth. Up to one million people are believed to be waiting for a cellular telephone line in the city.
Analysts noted BCP's tariff structure, which is only slightly cheaper than rates offered by existing monopoly Telesp, enabled the group to bid so high.
Peon told reporters BCP would begin providing cellular services within 12 months, covering all of Sao Paulo's 64 municipalities where about 17 million people live.

The task of installing a digital, Time Division Multiple Access system, made by Canada's Northern Telecom, would be made easier by Sao Paulo's predominance of skyscrapers which would serve as ready-built towers for antennae, he added.

Also Wednesday, another group, led by Brazilian textiles group Vicunha and Italian state-owned telecommunications company Stet, signed up for a smaller concession in the northeastern states of Bahia and Sergipe.

Brazil's Communications Ministry was due to announce Friday the winners of two further B Band concessions, one covering the remainder of Sao Paulo state and other several states in the less developed northeast.
A group named BCE, which also comprises BellSouth and Banco Safra, is among bidders for the northeastern concession.
The B Band program represents the first step of the Brazilian govenrment's plan to privatize the country's vast telecommunications industry.
Earlier Wednesday Communications Minister Sergio Motta reiterated his prediction that the federally owned Telebras system would be fully sold off by mid-1998.
